rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Spherical lenses** refract light twice: convex lenses converge (f > 0), concave lenses diverge (f < 0). The **lens formula** $\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$ with $m = v/u$ locates and sizes images; real images form on the far side and are inverted.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - 1/v − 1/u = 1/f - m = v/u = h'/h - Simple microscope: m = 1 + D/f (near point); m ≈ D/f (relaxed)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Sign Convention: Light travels left to right. Distances measured from optical centre. Object distance u is negative (object on left), focal length f positive for convex, negative for concave.  ·  Thin Lens Approximation: Lens formulas assume thin lens (thickness negligible compared to radii and object/image distances).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The angular magnification of a simple microscope is 1 + D/f with the image at the near point."

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Lens vs mirror formula:** 1/v − 1/u = 1/f for lenses; 1/v + 1/u = 1/f for mirrors — a minus-sign apart.  ·  **Real image through a lens forms on the far side** — light actually passes through the lens.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Lens Formula A lens bends light twice — once entering, once leaving — and the combined effect focuses rays to an image. The lens formula $\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$, its magnification $m = v/u$, and the angular magnification of a magnifier make up the working toolkit of all simple optics.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 Spherical lenses A **spherical lens** has two spherical refracting surfaces. **Convex (converging)** lenses are thicker in the middle; **concave (diverging)** lenses thinner. Key points: optical centre O, principal foci F and F′, focal length f (positive for convex, negative for concave).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "1/v = 1/f + 1/u with signs; m = v/u carries the sign of the image."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (4m): A convex lens of f = 12 cm forms a real image 3× the object's size. Find u and v.** — m = −3 → v = 3u (signs: u = −x, v = 3x). 1/(3x) + 1/x = 1/12 → 4/(3x) = 1/12 → x = 16 cm. Object 16 cm in front, image 48 cm behind.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: State image nature (real/virtual, erect/inverted) after every lens numerical.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **A lens refracts twice** — the formula sums the two surface effects.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f; m = v/u; angular magnification m = 1 + D/f (near point).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The eye's own lens changes focal length (accommodation) to keep images on the retina — a variable-focus lens.
